'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[United Nations]] calls on [[Ethiopia]] to grant them access to the [[Tigray region]] to investigate reports of [[mass murder]]s and [[sexual violence]] that may amount to [[war crime]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/4/un-ethiopian-eritrean-troops-behind-possible-war-crimes (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
* Archbishop [[Cesare Nosiglia]] of [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Turin|Turin, Italy]] announces that for the second time, the [[Shroud of Turin]] will be exposed for veneration on social media and websites on [[Holy Saturday]], April 3. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/shroud-of-turin-to-go-on-virtual-display-for-holy-saturday-84580 (Catholic News Agency)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 TAF AS532 crash]]
**An [[Turkish Land Forces|army]] helicopter crashes in [[Bitlis Province|Bitlis]], [[Turkey]], killing 11 [[Turkish Armed Forces|military]] personnel and injuring two others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/4/military-helicopter-crash-in-southeast-turkey-kills-ten (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The [[Robert Koch Institute]]'s [[Standing Committee on Vaccination]] officially approves the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for people aged over 65. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-56275342 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****The [[Government of Hungary|government]] orders all schools and non-essential shops in [[Hungary]] to close from March 8 until March 22 (for non-essential shops) and April 7 (for schools) due to a third wave of [[COVID-19]] infections. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/hungary-toughens-covid-19-lockdown-to-curb--very-strong--third-wave/46420030 (Swiss Info)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Prime Minister of Malta|Prime Minister]] [[Robert Abela]] announces that the [[Government of Malta|government]] will limit indoor gatherings to four households and will ban mass gatherings other than weddings and religious activities beginning tomorrow due to a record increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. The government will also restrict the operation of restaurants and snack bars to only offer takeaway services. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/abela-to-address-press-conference-as-covid-pressure-mounts.855664 (''Times of Malta'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports its first cases of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]] in two people from [[Ivano-Frankivsk]]. [https://covid.unian.info/covid-19-two-cases-of-uk-strain-officially-confirmed-in-ukraine-11341670.html (UNIAN)]
***[[European Commission–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine dispute]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] invokes the [[European Union]] powers to block shipment of 250,700 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine to [[Australia]] amid escalations between the bloc and [[AstraZeneca]]. The [[European Commission]] endorses the move. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/04/europe/italy-astrazeneca-doses-australia-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Prime Minister]] [[Hun Sen]] receives a dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied by the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/cambodian-prime-minister-hun-sen-inoculated-against-covid-19/2021/03/03/e0cc6acc-7ca2-11eb-8c5e-32e47b42b51b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****[[Kuwait]]'s [[37th Cabinet of Kuwait|Cabinet]] decides to impose a curfew from 5:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time for the next month but will allow salons, gyms, and other commercial activities to reopen on March 7 subject to operating restrictions. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/covid-19-kuwait-imposes-partial-curfew-starting-sunday-for-a-month---state-tv-1.1614878985693 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] receives its first shipment of 487,200 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied by the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-philippines-vaccin/philippines-receives-its-first-astrazeneca-vaccines-under-covax-idUSKBN2AW1MS (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]]'s National Medicines Regulatory Authority approves the use of [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine, becoming the second vaccine to be made available for the general public. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/sri-lanka-approves-russias-sputnik-v-vaccine/article33987742.ece (''The Hindu'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lesotho]]
****[[Lesotho]] receives its first shipment of 36,000 doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] manufactured by the [[Serum Institute of India]] through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/africa/2021-03-04-lesotho-receives-first-batch-of-vaccines/ (SowetanLIVE)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] becomes the first country in [[Africa]] to approve [[India]]'s [[Covaxin]] vaccine manufactured by [[Bharat Biotech]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/zimbabwe-approves-covaxin-first-in-africa-to-okay-india-made-covid-19-vaccine-101614859597880.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****Nine great [[ape]]s in [[San Diego Zoo]] becomes the first non-human primates to receive an experimental COVID-19 vaccine. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-03-04/san-diego-zoo-vaccinates-apes-against-covid-19 (''The Los Angeles Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Maine]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant that originated in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.newscentermaine.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/maine-cdc-confirms-first-case-of-covid-19-variant-b1351-first-detected-in-south-africa-confirmed-in-maine/97-481b481a-f049-4156-9593-55592b3d7c91 (WCSH-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] reports a record 1,910 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the last 24 hours, bringing the national death toll to 259,271. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/brazil-sees-record-high-covid-19-deaths-two-days-in-a-row-toll-at-259-271-121030400448_1.html (''Business Standard'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[United States Capitol Police]] requests that the [[United States National Guard|National Guard]] remain at the Capitol for 60 days in response to a possible second attack on the building. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/capitol-police-national-guard-stay-60-days/story?id=76254418 (ABC News)]
*Police in [[Bignona]], [[Senegal]], open fire against a group of people demonstrating against the arrest of opposition leader [[Ousmane Sonko]], killing a protester. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/4/senegal-clashes-kill-one-after-opposition-leader-arrest (Al Jazeera)]
*Twenty people are killed and others are feared dead after [[people smuggling|smugglers]] intentionally throw 80 [[Human migration|migrant]]s overboard during a voyage from [[Djibouti]] to [[Yemen]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/4/dozens-of-migrants-heading-to-yemen-thrown-overboard-feared-dead (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[The Troubles]], [[Brexit and the Irish border]]
**The [[Loyalist Communities Council]] and other loyalist groups in [[Northern Ireland]] inform [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] that they are withdrawing support for the [[Good Friday Agreement]] in opposition to the [[Northern Ireland Protocol]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/northern-ireland-loyalists-pull-support-for-good-friday-peace-deal/a-56766549 (DW)]
*The [[Government of India|Indian government's]] [[Income Tax Department]] raids the residences of the founders of [[Phantom Films]] due to allegations of [[tax evasion]]. Those being interrogated include [[Anurag Kashyap]], [[Taapsee Pannu]], [[Vikas Bahl]], [[Vikramaditya Motwane]], and [[Madhu Mantena]]. The incident prompts the [[Maha Vikas Aghadi]] alliance and [[Rahul Gandhi]] to support the film stars who are being [[interrogated]], saying the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] is using all the arms of the government to stifle the voices of those who support the [[2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest|Indian farmers' protest]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/after-raids-on-anurag-kashyap-taapsee-pannu-others-tax-officials-claim-crores-hidden-2383788 (NDTV)] [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/rahul-gandhi-uses-hindi-idioms-to-attack-centre-after-raids-on-taapsee-pannu-anurag-kashyap-2383394 (NDTV<sup>2</sup>)]
*Italian [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] secretary [[Nicola Zingaretti]] resigns, citing infighting over government posts. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-politics-zingaretti/italys-democratic-party-chief-zingaretti-resigns-decrying-infighting-idUSKCN2AW2G5?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[North Dakota House of Representatives]] votes to expel State Representative [[Luke Simons]] (R) following allegations that he threatened and sexually harassed women going back to 2017, when he first took office. This is the first time that either chamber of the [[North Dakota Legislative Assembly]] has passed such a vote. [https://apnews.com/article/north-dakota-f6d9a0aab71fde5d681b41443541449a (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]], [[2021 Pakistan Super League]]
**[[Pakistan]] suspends its [[Twenty20]] cricket competition in the [[Pakistan Super League]] after seven players tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20210304-pakistan-super-league-cricket-suspended-over-coronavirus-cases (RFI)]
